function.description: Preview a token swap WITHOUT executing - route, output, price impact, token safety. EVM routes to KyberSwap ONLY; "solana" → Jupiter, which requires JUPITER_API_KEY and answers `configuration_unavailable` if missing. EVM tokens must be a CONTRACT ADDRESS (resolve a symbol with TokenFind first) or native ETH/native; Solana a symbol or mint. `amountIn` is the HUMAN decimal of tokenIn. Call this BEFORE SwapExecute: a fresh quote (same venue) authorizes SwapExecute ONLY; every other authorizes its own. A ROUTE BEING AVAILABLE DOES NOT MEAN THE WALLET CAN PAY FOR IT: each quote reads the selected wallet into an `eligibility` block, and only `eligibility.executable` true authorizes an execute. The three balance outcomes are DISTINCT facts with distinct remedies. `insufficient_balance` means the wallet holds less of the input token than the trade needs; it names required, current and missing. `gas_reserve_insufficient` means native cannot cover the swap's TOTAL NATIVE DEBIT: every transaction it would broadcast, including the L1 data fee where the chain charges one, plus a measured reserve for one more transaction afterwards. `balance_unavailable` means a balance could not be READ, which is never the same statement as the wallet being short and always fails closed. On Solana only initialized, non-frozen token accounts count as spendable, so a FROZEN holding is present and NOT spendable. An ineligible quote still returns its route and is recorded, so a later execute cannot fall back on an older funded quote. Every balance figure here is a QUOTE-TIME OBSERVATION, advisory and ageing: the authoritative read happens again immediately before each signature, so an execute can still refuse for balance after this call said executable. Fee already inside the route: EVM `extraFee - THE VEX FEE, 25 bps of the input token`; Solana `feePreview`, the same 25 bps Vex fee, taken inside the Jupiter route. KyberSwap is the primary swap venue; if it cannot route the pair, quote SwapQuoteUniswap instead. Full contract: vex_ToolDescribe.
function.name: SwapQuote

amountIn.description: Amount of tokenIn to swap, in HUMAN decimal units (e.g. "1.5"). Not wei/lamports.

chain.description: Chain to swap on. EVM slugs/aliases route to KyberSwap (ethereum, base, arbitrum, robinhood, …); the literal "solana" routes to Jupiter. Accepts a chain slug/alias or the numeric chain id TokenFind returns (e.g. base or 8453).

slippageBps.description: Slippage tolerance in basis points (1 bps = 0.01%); default 100 = 1%, which fits deep, liquid pairs. It is the ONLY price protection on the trade. Pass the SAME value to the quote and the execute, or omit it on both - a mismatch blocks the execute. On a thin or volatile pair (new listings, memecoins, small pools) 100 bps often fails. When it fails, the message says so and names this parameter: re-quote with a higher slippageBps and pass the same value to the execute. Do not read a slippage failure as "this pair is untradeable" and do not switch venue for it - another venue at 100 bps fails the same way. Vex caps it at 1000 (10%) and REJECTS anything above rather than clamping; every increase widens the worst-case price you accept, so raise it in steps.

tokenIn.description: Input token. EVM: the token CONTRACT ADDRESS or native ETH/native. For an EVM token, call TokenFind with exactly one target chain and continue only when mutationReady is true. Ambiguous, provider-capped, or metadata-unreadable results are not executable identities. If the swap pair is already known, prefer its exact base or quote token address and use TokenFind to validate that address on the target chain. TokenFind reads symbol and decimals from the contract, never provider list metadata. Solana: symbol or mint.
